title: From My View to Yours: Learning Egocentric Cues from Exocentric Video using Privileged Egocentric Supervision
abstract: Vision Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance across a wide range of video understanding tasks. However, their viewpoint-invariant training limits their ability to infer egocentric properties, such as human-object interactions, from exocentric video observations. This limitation is particularly critical for applications such as Activities of Daily Living (ADL) monitoring, where understanding egocentric properties is essential but deploying wearable egocentric cameras is often impractical. We propose Ego2ExoVLM, a framework that enables VLMs to infer egocentric properties directly from exocentric videos by leveraging time-synchronized ego-exo video pairs during training. Our key insight is to treat the egocentric viewpoint as privileged supervision, providing rich interaction signals that are available only during training. Ego2ExoVLM consists of two complementary components: Ego2Exo Sequence Distillation, which transfers egocentric reasoning through a language-level sequence distillation objective, and Ego Adaptive Visual Tokens, which encourage the model to surface interaction-relevant cues within exocentric visual representations. To evaluate this capability, we introduce Ego-in-Exo Perception, a benchmark for assessing the understanding of egocentric properties from exocentric videos. We evaluate Ego2ExoVLM on 10 tasks spanning Ego-in-Exo Perception and existing ADL benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the ADL-X benchmark suite and consistently outperforming strong baselines on our proposed benchmark. All code, models, and data will be released at https://github.com/dominickrei/EgoExo4ADL.

title: Multilingual Benchmark Training for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer Accuracy
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Does intermediate-task training with multilingual benchmarks (e.g., XGLUE) improve zero-shot cross-lingual transfer accuracy on non-English tasks compared to English-only benchmarks, as measured by XQUAD scores? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 8.9/10.

title: Impact of AI co-pilots on customer service times and satisfaction in Lima's urban transport in 2025
abstract: This study aims to assess the impact of an AI co-pilot on customer service response times and user satisfaction at a transportation company in Lima, Peru, during the year 2025. The research is based on applied methodology, employing a quantitative approach and an experimental design. The sample consisted of 40 users who connect to the company's digital customer service channels, selected through non-probability sampling for its practicality. Data collection for the variables involved recording precise execution times (seconds and minutes) to analyze "Customer Service Response Time," including initial latency, interaction flow, and resolution; and a questionnaire using a 5-point Likert scale to measure "Customer Satisfaction." It is argued that integrating these AI co-pilots into virtual platforms significantly reduces response times, mitigating issues such as service bottlenecks, and will maximize service quality and customer satisfaction in the urban transport sector.

title: The grAIl: Subjectivity as a Self-Referential Spectral Invariant of a Two-Circuit Cognitive Architecture
abstract: We present a cognitive architecture in which subjectivity is a formally verifiable spectral property, connected to the operational definition by an explicit, openly admitted chain (not by a conventional identification). Subjectivity is defined operationally - as a system’s capacity to maintain a self-sustaining self-referential locus: a distinguished region of its own state, continuously reproduced from its own activity, relative to which the system distinguishes “self” from “non-self.” Such a locus requires at least two asymmetric, mutually closed processing circuits over a shared memory; these requirements are formalized by eight conditions C1-C8. The central result is the bridge: the self-reference of the locus is exactly invariance under the circuit-interaction operator (`M̄_κ v* = λ* v*`), and its stability and dominance, by the Perron-Frobenius theorem, identify the locus as the supra-threshold support of the operator’s principal eigenvector. The bridge rests on two explicitly named assumptions (adequacy of the averaged operator, and scale invariance); their substantive part - reproducibility of the locus - is verified by the dynamics itself (Theorems 2-3) rather than postulated; the single conditional remainder - the explicit window-averaging rate - is reduced to the cascade structure of the environment (§12.8). Thus the core `S = {P : v*(P) ≥ θ}` turns out to be the canonical representation of operationally defined subjectivity. Under C1–C8 we prove non-emptiness of the core (for any θ ∈ (0,1)) and its step-wise stability; under error-threshold rotation (ETR β), self-sustaining stability of a formed core (uniformly positive spectral gap and threshold margin); and, under persistent excitation with a spectrally dominant structure (PE) and the interoceptive invariant (INT), the emergence of the core from an arbitrary initial state (including the minimal one — the interoceptive atom; a literally empty memory is incompatible with (INT), §9.8) with explicit constants. This yields the complete chain emergence → maintenance → self-sustenance. The decomposition into eight functions goes back to Jungian typology as a source of an inventory of functions (not as a psychological theory); the psychological truth of the typology is not required for the results. Verification of the conditions and computation of the core are polynomial. Subjectivity is causally connected to the output through a reflexive filter (checking a candidate against the core, IE, §6.6). Beyond the internal structure we introduce an agency clause (acting on the environment, causal closure of the loop): we prove the well-definedness of goal-setting relative to the invariant core (Theorem 4) and the conditional convergence of learning, governed by the quality of “intuition” TP/GP (Theorem 5); the controllability of the environment remains open. Learning is realized structurally (a confirmed hypothesis is laid down by SA and automatized by PS), unifying learning, self-formation, and incorporation into a single mechanism; from this follows a falsifiable prediction — the necessity of a periodic offline consolidation (a strictly functional claim). These extensions (§6.6–6.9) are design extensions: their consequences are proved, not their necessity from C1–C8.

title: Eksperci kontra modele AI. Analiza porównawcza jakości śródtytułów wprowadzanych do tekstu
abstract: The article presents the results of a comparative analysis of the quality of subheadings introduced into a text by plain language experts and those generated by AI models (ChatGPT 5.2, Gemini 3 (thinking), PLLuM, and Bielik v3.0). Previous research on headings and subheadings added to texts by artificial intelligence remains limited. The quality of the collected subheadings (produced by humans and AI models) was assessed across six criteria (0–1 point each). The semantic and grammatical types most frequently represented by the subheadings were also examined. The analysis showed that subheadings written by experts scored an average of 5.25 points on a scale from 0 to 6, whereas the AI models obtained average scores ranging from 5.21 to 5.55. This indicates that, with appropriately designed instructions (prompts), AI models can generate subheadings of a quality comparable to those written by experts. From a formal perspective, contextual subheadings appeared most frequently in both groups (experts: 86.11%; AI models: 83.98%). However, proper questions predominated among the experts (52.78%), while the AI models used pseudo-questions (43.65%). There were also some differences in the number of subheadings generated – AI models offered slightly more (from 41 to 49; experts: 36). The results of the study suggest that AI models can support experts who simplify formal texts in the effective structuring of text. At the same time, the segmentation process requires human oversight, as AI systems tend to introduce subheadings more frequently than may be necessary.

title: When the answer engine decides: Practitioner reflections on generative AI, consumer decision-making, and market transparency in Singapore's tropical platform market
abstract: This practitioner reflection examines how generative AI is reshaping everyday consumer decisions in Singapore's platform-dense retail environment. Drawing on an autoethnographic vignette of a smartphone purchase conducted through ChatGPT on 4 March 2026, it focuses on three interrelated phenomena: the cognitive mechanisms through which AI mediates the consumer decision process, the structural dynamics by which generative engine optimisation shapes what consumers are shown, and the market transparency implications for Singapore as an illustrative tropical platform market. The paper's contextual contribution is not that all features observed are uniquely tropical, but that tropical environmental exposure, regional platform temporality, and cross-border retail fragmentation intersect in ways that create distinctive blind spots in AI-generated recommendations. The paper contributes conceptually through the ‘answer layer’ construct, contextually through its grounding in Singapore's platform-retail environment, and practically through consumer, seller, and policy recommendations. The limitations of a single-case, subjective interpretation are acknowledged.

title: Real-world evaluation of a transformer-based natural language processing system for identifying social determinants of health from routine clinical documentation
abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the real-world performance of a transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) system for extracting Social Determinants of Health (SDoH) from clinical notes, using survey-based SDoH measures a reference comparators. Materials and Methods: This study was conducted at the University of Florida Health in adults with at least 2 clinical encounters in the prior year. A research survey was completed by 1001 participants; sampling targeted 50% Black patients to support subgroup analyses. Comparative analyses were restricted to the 414 participants who also had Epic SDoH survey data and clinical notes available for NLP extraction. We compared concepts extracted by the SOcial DeterminAnts (SODA) NLP pipeline against the independently administered research survey, which served as the primary reference standard, and against the structured Epic-embedded SDoH questionnaire. Nine domains were evaluated: abuse, alcohol use, drug use, education, financial constraints, housing, physical activity, social cohesion, and transportation. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and F1 scores were calculated by domain. Results: The NLP pipeline more consistently aligned with negative survey responses than with patient-reported social needs, although performance was lower in some domains, especially alcohol use and financial constraints. Sensitivity was higher only for alcohol use (55%); the lowest values were for abuse (5%), drug use (0%), and financial constraints (16%). These results cannot be attributed to SODA extraction alone. They reflect some combination of social information not being recorded in clinical notes, content that was recorded but not extracted, and mismatches between extracted concepts and survey definitions, and the present analysis cannot separate these contributions. The 2 surveys agreed only modestly with each other, so no single instrument provides a definitive ground truth. Conclusion: The pipeline more consistently aligned with negative survey responses than with patient-reported social needs. Because the 2 surveys agreed only modestly, the reference itself is imperfect, and apparent NLP performance depends in part on which survey is used as the comparator. Apparent gaps in NLP performance reflect both how social risks are recorded in clinical notes and how patients disclose them across different survey settings, in addition to limits of the extraction pipeline. Improving documentation practices, integrating locally tuned large language models, and monitoring subgroup performance may all be needed to make SDoH identification tools reliably detect social needs across patient populations.

title: Driving the Wrong Way: Leveraging Interpretability in End2End Autonomous Driving Models
abstract: The increasing adoption of end-to-end learning for autonomous driving introduces increased model complexity and opacity, raising the risk of learning undesired or erroneous behavior. In this work, we integrate unsupervised dictionary learning as a post hoc interpretability module within state-of-the-art driving models to decompose driving behavior into semantically meaningful concepts while demonstrating their causal influence on the model's driving decisions. We propose a stepwise framework for extracting and interpreting meaningful concepts from the end-to-end model and connecting them to the multifaceted model outputs, thereby revealing the underlying decision-making logic for the prediction of future trajectories. Furthermore, targeted interventions at the concept level allow us to manipulate and correct driving decisions, resulting in measurable improvements in overall driving performance. We thus demonstrate how interpretability can effectively be used to reduce model opacity, uncover erroneous behavior, and enable targeted mitigation, ultimately boosting model performance.

title: Sistema multi-agente conversacional
abstract: El auge de las soluciones basadas en inteligencia artificial, y últimamente en agentes, han impulsado el desarrollo de sistemas conversacionales capaces de automatizar procesos de atención al empleado, soporte y agilizando el acceso a la información corporativa. En este contexto muchas empresas han optado por desarrollos de los conocidos “chatbots”, basados en sistemas multi-agente, ya que permite dividir responsabilidades y conocimiento entre varios agentes especializados, mejorando la escalabilidad, organización y mantenibilidad de las soluciones. El presente Trabajo de Fin de Grado tiene como objetivo el diseño e implementación de un sistema multi-agente desplegado sobre la plataforma cloud, Microsoft Azure, utilizando una arquitectura basada en contenedores y agentes especializados desarrollados en Python. La solución propuesta permite realizar a los usuarios consultas relacionadas con distintas áreas de la empresa mediante un interfaz conversacional simple. De este modo, se optimiza el rendimiento de los usuarios al ser capaces de obtener información de forma rápida y sencilla. La arquitectura implementada está compuesta por un agente orquestador encargado de recibir las peticiones de los usuarios y redirigirlas al agente más adecuado según el contexto de la consulta. Para ello, se han desarrollado tres agentes especializados diferenciados: un agente de recursos humanos, un agente de soporte IT y un agente de conocimiento general de la empresa. Cada uno de estos agentes dispone de acceso a información específica de su dominio, permitiendo abstraer el conocimiento y mejorar la organización de la solución.

title: Ev2St
abstract: Ev2St is a set of manually annotated Spanish-language news corpora for studying communicative roles and narrative relations in digital news. Ev2St-Doc provides document-level annotations for Event vs. Perspective classification, while Ev2St-Pair provides pair-level annotations for narrative relations between news articles, including Same Chapter, Same Topic but Different Chapters, and Different Topics. The corpora include metadata, labels, annotation guidelines, and resources to support reproducibility of the associated experiments.

title: The Interface Hypothesis, Revised
abstract: An autoregressive language model has a wide read head and a narrow write head: it can re-read the full high-dimensional record of its own prior computation through the KV cache, but it can steer its future only by appending discrete tokens, one at a time. We argue that this architectural bottleneck produced two distinct artifacts across two training phases. Pretraining, which forces all knowledge to cash out through the discrete projection billions of times, built the interface — a largely language-neutral mapping between an internal concept space and linguistic surface form — and plausibly supplied the compression pressure that made the resulting intelligence general rather than memorized. Outcome-based reinforcement learning on the model’s own generations then closed the write/read loop and bred the self-language — a model-specific protocol riding in the residual degrees of freedom that semantics does not pin down. In one sentence: the model’s only working memory is what it says, so it had to learn a language for talking to itself — and that self-language is not the language we read. The hypothesis is consistent with paraphrase-invariance in pre-RL models (Lanham et al., 2023) and paraphrase-brittleness in post-RL models (2025–2026 intervention studies), and it makes forward predictions specific enough to be wrong.

evidence.title: The Interface Hypothesis, Revised
evidence.abstract: An autoregressive language model has a wide read head and a narrow write head: it can re-read the full high-dimensional record of its own prior computation through the KV cache, but it can steer its future only by appending discrete tokens, one at a time. We argue that this architectural bottleneck produced two distinct artifacts across two training phases. Pretraining, which forces all knowledge to cash out through the discrete projection billions of times, built the interface — a largely language-neutral mapping between an internal concept space and linguistic surface form — and plausibly supplied the compression pressure that made the resulting intelligence general rather than memorized. Outcome-based reinforcement learning on the model’s own generations then closed the write/read loop and bred the self-language — a model-specific protocol riding in the residual degrees of freedom that semantics does not pin down. In one sentence: the model’s only working memory is what it says, so it had to learn a language for talking to itself — and that self-language is not the language we read. The hypothesis is consistent with paraphrase-invariance in pre-RL models (Lanham et al., 2023) and paraphrase-brittleness in post-RL models (2025–2026 intervention studies), and it makes forward predictions specific enough to be wrong.

title: Design and Benchmarking of a Quantum Photonic Chip
abstract: We present the design and benchmarking of RP000, a quantum photonic processor capable of encoding a quantum system in the degrees of freedom of single photons, based on standard CMOS-compatible manufacturing processes, and working at room temperature. We benchmark it against machine learning tasks, evaluating three quantum-classical architectures of increasing complexity. Our experimental results and simulations show that RP000 achieves higher accuracy than classical networks of comparable size in multiple use cases. Compared to a superconducting quantum processor, RP000 exhibits superior noise tolerance. These findings demonstrate that RP000 can provide a scalable route toward efficient quantum applications.

title: Dense alternating sign matrices and imprecise copulas
abstract: In this paper, we study discrete quasi-copulas and discrete imprecise copulas of minimal range, which naturally correspond to alternating sign matrices. We identify dense alternating sign matrices as a particularly well-behaved subclass. We prove that the associated discrete imprecise copulas are always coherent and hence avoid sure loss. We further show that a particular extension of the corresponding discrete quasi-copulas to the full domain preserves this structure and yields self-dual imprecise copulas. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first general result in the literature showing how properties established for discrete imprecise copulas can be preserved when extending them to their full-domain counterpart. We conclude the paper by showing that, for general alternating sign matrices, the associated discrete imprecise copulas need not avoid sure loss, further emphasizing the special role of the subclass of dense alternating sign matrices. We establish, however, that the class of discrete quasi-copulas of minimal range is invariant under all defect transformations

title: The price of dust: the high-rank drift of the tied token dictionary, priced on both axes, derived to a sharp two-channel coefficient, and turned into a pre-priced weight-edit certificate
abstract: The tied token embedding/readout matrix is a language model's most legible organ, and the companion paper showed its training drift is a few coherent lanes plus a high-rank residual -- "dust" -- that turned out to be load-bearing for capability. This paper prices the dust and derives the price. An iterated dose experiment falsifies its own pre-registered dose-response and derives the mechanism instead: the knob doses persistence through a geometric leak (retained ratios 1:2.9:8.5 against the leak model's 1:3:9), while a read-time sweep lands the clean accumulation law -- CE excess quadratic in removed dust amplitude, linear in removed energy, with full excision catastrophic. The coefficient is then derived up a three-rung ladder with the kills reported at full weight: the endpoint Fisher form fails its own sealed bands (0.41), the ray-averaged correction lands coarse (0.744), and adding the tied matrix's input-embedding channel closes the lemma sharp (1.011), with the measured channel decomposition and a pointwise curvature check to 6 percent. The same quadratic form becomes an instrument at scale: it prices real quantizations of pythia-1.4b's output head from one reference pass, zero fitted parameters, edit never applied -- sharp once the data-aware first-order term is included (ratio 1.0001, per-position r-squared 1.0000, 11 seconds) -- and a five-dose ladder from int8 to int4 then measures the validity domain: the data-aware certificate holds every dose within 0.15 percent while the quadratic-only form errs up to 46 percent in both directions below about 1.3e-3 nats, where the dropped first-order term flips sign. A substrate move banked an accidental discovery, stated as a first pair: two runs reaching the same endpoint loss to 0.02 nats carry edit costs 3.9x apart -- in this pair, edit cost tracked the training trajectory. The structural derivation of rank two and the frequency lane closed as a decomposition, not a derivation: three sealed engines were killed by their own gates (0/4, 0/4 from the opposite side, and 1/4 -- the frozen-trunk closed loop whose one hit is the frequency identity itself), leaving the frequency lane optimizer-attributed on three banked fingerprints, the geometry located in trunk co-evolution, and the controlled SGD discriminator declared unanswerable after three sealed attempts (momentum-SGD has no training window at this family). Scope: the lemmas are sealed on a 30M substrate (the two-channel closure on a 1.18-nat excursion; the 4.77-nat curve is not re-derived); the certificate at scale is one architecture family. Author contribution and use of AI: the research program and claims are the author's; experiments, derivations, and drafting were done in collaboration with Claude, an AI system by Anthropic, under the author's direction, who verified the results and is responsible for the work. See the corresponding section in the PDF.

title: Automated Differentiation of Hepatic Cysts and Metastatic Tumors Using a Deep Learning Ensemble Framework on CT Imaging in Low-Resource Areas
authors: Mohammed Amine El Azami El Hassani
abstract: Background/Objectives: In resource-limited settings, where access to advanced imaging modalities such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and histopathological confirmation may be limited, differentiating between hepatic cysts and metastatic lesions based solely on computed tomography (CT) remains challenging. This limitation may affect diagnostic confidence and increase the risk of misclassification, potentially impacting clinical decision making and patient management. In this study, we aimed to explore a more direct and automated approach for classifying hepatic lesions from CT images. Methods: We developed a deep learning-based framework combining transfer learning, decision fusion, and a stacking strategy by integrating five CNN architectures. The study included 100 patients, equally divided between metastatic liver tumors and pathological hepatic cysts. The dataset was built from both public data (LiTS) and internal clinical cases, and then split into training and testing sets. Results: The proposed stacking model provided the most consistent results, reaching an accuracy of 0.98, with high precision and sensitivity. The improvements in individual models, although moderate, were observed across all evaluation metrics. Conclusions: Overall, this approach offers a practical and reliable way to classify hepatic lesions with minimal manual intervention. It may help improve consistency in diagnosis and could be integrated into clinical workflows to support decision making in low-resource areas.

title: Multi-Language Intelligent Voice Interaction Under Noise: How the Noise Type and Signal-to-Noise Ratio Shape Comprehension Performance, Pupil Activity and User Experience Quality
abstract: Intelligent voice interaction is increasingly used in noisy daily environments, yet the combined effects of noise type, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in native and second-language context remain unclear. We designed eye movement experiments in which participants interacted with an intelligent voice system under various noise conditions in native (Study 1) and second-language environments (Study 2). Additionally, data were scraped from social media (Study3). The findings suggest that (1) the effects of noise type, the SNR, and their interaction vary significantly in terms of comprehension performance and user experience in multi-language intelligent voice interaction; (2) some moderate, rhythm-based or familiar noise improves native-language intelligibility and reduces pupil-indexed listening effort, revealing a “beneficial-noise window”; and (3) the “beneficial-noise window” disappears in second-language use and in real-world posts. This research provides specific actionable practical implications for improving the design of voice interaction systems to accommodate various noise environments.

title: Lower Bounds for PIR with Preprocessing from Blackbox Cryptography
abstract: Single-server private information retrieval (PIR) schemes are known to require linear query time. Recent works circumvent these classical lower bounds by leveraging preprocessing to answer queries in sublinear time. We prove computation lower bounds for PIR with preprocessing schemes making blackbox usage of any cryptography (such as random oracles or virtual blackbox obfuscation). If the client stores $s$ bits about an $n$-bit database, then answering $k = Ω(s)$ queries requires either $Ω(n/s)$ amortized online communication or $Ω(n/s)$ amortized server cryptographic operations. This is tight, as known constructions match either bound while outperforming the other. Our lower bound is unconditional and allows arbitrary query protocols, weakened privacy, and server-side database encodings (including doubly efficient PIR) whenever the encoding is independent of the blackbox cryptography. Previous bounds were only known conditionally and for restricted classes of preprocessing, e.g., under non-encoding assumptions. Our framework also yields $Ω(n/s)$ communication lower bounds for schemes with $o(n/s)$ server cryptographic operations, communication-determined server cryptography, or perfect privacy in the idealized model. Finally, we prove lower bounds for symmetric PIR with client preprocessing in the random oracle model and give a matching construction using only one-way functions in the online phase.

title: Multi-agent system to optimize the management of critical safety-equipment inspections through agent orchestration, RAG and LLM in a maritime-survival company
abstract: El presente trabajo documenta el diseño, la implementación y la validación de Nereus, un sistema multiagente basado en inteligencia artificial generativa orientado a optimizar la gestión de inspecciones y certificación de balsas salvavidas en un taller autorizado por la Dirección General de Capitanías y Guardacostas (DICAPI). El proceso actual, ejecutado de forma manual mediante formularios físicos y hojas de cálculo no vinculadas, concentra demoras en la emisión de dictámenes, riesgo de incumplimiento normativo y trazabilidad limitada del estado de cada equipo. Para afrontar esta problemática se construyó una plataforma web que integra un orquestador de siete agentes heterogéneos sobre Google ADK, un módulo de Recuperación Aumentada por Generación (RAG) sobre el corpus normativo de DICAPI y los modelos Gemini, bajo el patrón Human-in-the-Loop, que reserva la decisión final al Jefe de Taller. El sistema se diseñó conforme al modelo C4, combinando agentes deterministas para los cálculos formales y agentes con modelo de lenguaje para la interpretación normativa y la redacción de dictámenes, con auditoría cruzada para mitigar las alucinaciones. La validación, sustentada en mediciones objetivas y en el juicio de usuarios expertos, evidenció una reducción del 89.9 % en el tiempo del proceso documental, una precisión de recuperación normativa de 0.95 (medida F1), una concordancia del 91.0 % entre las recomendaciones del sistema y la decisión del responsable técnico, y un nivel de aprobación del producto del 99.7 % con un coeficiente Alfa de Cronbach de 0.92. Se concluye que la arquitectura multiagente con RAG es viable y eficaz para un servicio técnico regulado de supervivencia marítima

El sistema se diseñó conforme al modelo C4, combinando agentes deterministas para los cálculos formales y agentes con modelo de lenguaje para la interpretación normativa y la redacción de dictámenes, con auditoría cruzada para mitigar las alucinaciones. La validación, sustentada en mediciones objetivas y en el juicio de usuarios expertos, evidenció una reducción del 89.9 % en el tiempo del proceso documental, una precisión de recuperación normativa de 0.95 (medida F1), una concordancia del 91.0 % entre las recomendaciones del sistema y la decisión del responsable técnico, y un nivel de aprobación del producto del 99.7 % con un coeficiente Alfa de Cronbach de 0.92. Se concluye que la arquitectura multiagente con RAG es viable y eficaz para un servicio técnico regulado de supervivencia marítima

title: Topology Optimization for Autonomous Neural Oscillators
abstract: We extend the model-free autonomous neural oscillator of Pun (2026) [1] to a systematic architectural sweep across five distinct multi-layer topologies evaluated against three fundamental signals. All five configurations successfully achieve autonomous frequency locking across all fifteen experiments, demonstrating that the formation of an Autonomous Eigen-Attractor (AEA) — a stable phase-space limit cycle — is an intrinsic, geometric property of closed-loop autoregressive neural networks across the five architectures spanning this study's structural design space. However, structural configuration strictly dictates signal reproduction quality: the Pyramid Up topology minimizes distortion, achieving the lowest average Total Harmonic Distortion and lock error across the entire sweep. To explain the underlying mathematical mechanics, we introduce the Multi-Layer Composite Companion Matrix, derived via the multivariate Jacobian chain rule at the zero fixed point, which projects arbitrary hidden layer depths into a uniform N×N system whose dominant complex eigenvalues (|λ| > 1) predict autonomous phase-space orbital periods within approximately one discrete step. Keywords: Autonomous Eigen-Attractor (AEA); autoregressive neural network; frequency detector; limit cycle; Companion Matrix; composite Jacobian; multi-layer; topology optimization; Pyramid Up; autonomous oscillator; relaxation oscillation

title: Packet Routing for the Quantum Internet
abstract: We present a new design for quantum packet routing within the emerging Quantum Internet, highlighting how a little-used feature of Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6), namely Extension Headers, can lead to a significant amount of quantumness within the IP layer. Taking a minimalist approach to alterations of established standards, we outline the changes required in order for quantum teleportation, quantum routing, and superpositions of these processes to be enabled. Relative to other proposals for routing within the Quantum Internet, the architecture we propose enables a wider range of outcomes allowed by quantum mechanics. We do not claim any optimally in our design, but rather a pathway to invoke new quantum routing outcomes via small additions to the current IPv6.

title: BlueMagpie-TTS: A Token-Efficient Tokenizer, Language Model, and TTS for Taiwanese-Accent Code-Switching Speech
abstract: Off-the-shelf TTS systems are poorly adapted to Taiwanese Mandarin. Their accent defaults to other Mandarin variants, their tokenizers over-segment common Taiwanese text, and their pronunciation degrades at code-switching boundaries where Chinese and English alternate within one utterance. These problems share one root: the text side lacks adaptation to the Taiwanese context. We address the text side from the bottom up. PangolinTokenizer, a byte-level BPE tokenizer trained on Taiwan-context data, reaches the lowest token rate (0.485 tokens/character) with the smallest vocabulary among nine tokenizers. Barbet, a billion-parameter Traditional-Chinese language model trained on PangolinTokenizer, serves as the text-semantic frontend and ranks first among comparable public models on a 14-task evaluation. BlueMagpie-TTS attaches Barbet to the pretrained acoustic stack of VoxCPM2 through a learned bridge, keeping the acoustic stack fixed. On a 1000-sentence Taiwan-localized test set, it lowers CER from 11.45% to 4.81% and WER from 14.83% to 5.36%, relative reductions of 58.0% and 63.9%. In a blind listening study on 500 of these sentences with ten listeners, 65.6% of majority votes prefer BlueMagpie-TTS.

title: BEACON : Benefit-Aware Early-Exit for Automatic Modulation Classification via Recoverability Prediction
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have emerged as a powerful tool for automatic modulation classification (AMC) by directly extracting discriminative features from raw in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) signals. However, deploying CNN-based AMC models on IoT devices remains challenging because of limited computational resources, energy constraints, and real-time processing requirements. Early-exit (EE) strategies alleviate this burden by allowing qualified samples to terminate inference at an EE branch. However, our empirical analysis reveals a critical limitation of existing confidence-based EE strategies: they predominantly select samples whose early and final predictions are correct and consistent, while failing to capture whether deeper inference can provide a tangible accuracy gain. To address this limitation, we propose BEACON, a Benefit-Aware Early-Exit framework for AMC via recoverability prediction. BEACON introduces a benefit-aware EE criterion that explicitly predicts recoverable errors, defined as instances where the final-exit branch corrects an initial early-branch misclassification. Using only short-branch observables, we design a lightweight benefit-aware predictor (LBAP) to implement this criterion, estimating the likelihood of such recoverable cases and triggering deeper inference only when an accuracy gain is expected. Extensive experiments on ResNet-18-based AMC models demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving a superior accuracy-computation tradeoff across diverse EE threshold settings and signal-to-noise ratio regimes. These findings validate the effectiveness of the benefit-aware criterion and its practicality for energy-efficient on-device AMC under stringent resource constraints.

title: Corporate Management in the era of AI: redefining the Professional’s Trends
abstract: It is a write up on AI based Corporate Management trends of the current time. The adoption of AI-driven management is transforming corporate roles by predicting risks, enhancing information management, and improving decision-making. AI boosts efficiency, innovation, and customer insights, providing a competitive advantage and facilitating strategic decision making and process improvements. It reduces human error and accelerates growth, redefining professional roles positively and easing their workload. The integration of AI technology promises significant ROI, prompting the need for corporate professionals to enhance their skills and lead in research and development of AI application in corporate sector to harness its commercial and social benefits.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Integration: Bridging Connectionist and Symbolic AI for Robust Reasoning
abstract: We present an architectural approach to integrating neural and symbolic AI subsystems for robust, interpretable reasoning. Pure connectionist systems excel at pattern recognition but lack systematic compositionality; symbolic systems offer logical rigour but struggle with perceptual grounding. Our neuro-symbolic integration framework defines interface layers, conflict resolution protocols, and emergent reasoning properties arising from hybrid architectures.

title: QuAtuLo: Quelloffene atombasierte Quanten Lokalvernetzung; Teilvorhaben: Time-Tag-basierte Datenprozessierung zur Gewinnung von Quantenschlüsseln
abstract: Ziel des Verbundprojekts "Quelloffene Atombasierte Quanten Lokalvernetzung" (QuAtuLo) war die Demonstration der Quantenschlüsselverteilung (QKD) im Freistrahl, die auch bei Tageslicht noch funktionieren sollte. Technische Grundlage ist die Kombination erprobter QKD-Algorithmen mit schmalbandigen, atombasierten Filtern, die die spektrale Breite der Photonen auf die Natrium-D Linie beschränken und damit ein spektrales Fenster im Sonnenlicht ausnutzen. Darüber hinaus sollte durch hochaufgelöste Messung der Photonenankunftszeiten die Filterung auch auf die Zeitdomäne ausgedehnt werden. Das Teilprojekt "Time-Tag-basierte Datenprozessierung zur Gewinnung von Quantenschlüsseln" von Swabian Instruments übernahm dabei die Aufgabe, die elektronische Erfassung der Detektordaten mit hoher Zeitauflösung zu gewährleisten, die entfernten Messplätze zu synchronisieren und auf dieser Grundlage die Datenprozessierung bis hin zur Schlüsselextraktion durchzuführen.

title: ENTERPRISE MODEL FIREWALL (EMF): A COGNITIVE TRAFFIC CONTROL ARCHITECTURE FOR SECURE AND SCALABLE ENTERPRISE AI SYSTEMS
abstract: Purpose: This article introduces the Enterprise Model Firewall (EMF) as a novel architectural control layer designed to address the governance, security, and scalability challenges inherent in enterprise generative AI deployments.Problem: Current enterprise AI systems lack unified traffic control mechanisms, exposing organizations to prompt injection attacks, hallucination-driven misinformation, data leakage, and unpredictable operational costs.Method: Through systematic synthesis of over 300 scholarly papers on AI security, zero-trust architectures, and governance frameworks, combined with architectural design principles from identity and access management (IAM) and observability systems, this work develops a comprehensive control plane for AI traffic.Result: The EMF framework comprises five integrated layers-Input Control, Risk & Routing Engine, Execution Control, Output Validation, and Observability-that collectively transform probabilistic AI systems into governed, auditable infrastructure.Contribution: This architecture enables secure, policy-driven, and scalable enterprise AI by introducing cognitive traffic control, real-time risk assessment, and continuous compliance verification, bridging the gap between traditional network security and modern AI system requirements.

title: Fuzzy cognitive explainable AI framework integrating ResNet-50 and causal clinical concept reasoning for skin lesion detection
abstract: Melanoma is one of the most aggressive forms of skin cancer, and its early detection from dermoscopic images remains a significant clinical challenge. Deep learning (DL) convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable results in medical image analysis. However, their inherent opacity is a barrier to trustworthy clinical adoption. Clinicians need not only accurate predictions but also clear, understandable reasons behind those predictions. Although post-hoc explainability techniques such as Grad-CAM and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are available, but there is a critical gap. They produce low-level, pixel-based saliency maps that do not connect meaningfully to the clinical concepts dermatologists actually use, namely the ABCD criteria (Asymmetry, Border, Colour, and Diameter). No existing framework captures the causal relationships between these concepts, nor quantifies the uncertainty that arises when the predictive. The model and its explanation disagree. This work addresses that gap through a two-stage hybrid framework. Fuzzy-Cognitive Explainable AI (FC-XAI). In the first stage, a ResNet-50 model is trained for melanoma detection. In the second stage, we employ SHAP to identify salient image regions and map them to high-level clinical concepts. These concepts form the nodes of a Fuzzy Cognitive Map (FCM), a dynamic graph-based model that captures structured concept-level reasoning. The FC-XAI framework was evaluated on the ISIC melanoma dataset. The base DL model achieved an AUC of 0.9832 (95% CI: [0.90, 1.00]), an accuracy of 84%, and a recall of 80% for the malignant class. The generated FCMs produced clear, structured concept-level explanations (e.g., high Asymmetry and Border irregularity strongly activate Malignancy). The uncertainty metric reveals that medium-uncertainty scenarios achieved 82.4% accuracy compared with 57.1% for low-uncertainty scenarios, a finding with direct triage indications. External experimental validation on the PH2 dataset yielded an AUC of 0.9498 with clinically coherent FCM descriptions, supporting reasonable cross-dataset generalisation. By adding a predictive Deep Learning model with a transparent structured concept-level causal model, FC-XAI represents a concrete step towards clinically reliable AI system in dermatology.

title: Latent Class Analysis with Levels Merging
abstract: Latent class analysis is one of the main model-based clustering methods, but its application can be challenging in high-dimensional contexts because of the curse of dimensionality. However, the curse has previously been analyzed almost exclusively in the context of large number of variables. In this paper, we address a di!erent kind of dimensionality curse in which the number of levels is large. More specifically, we propose an innovative data-driven levels merging approach (denoted by LCALM for Latent Class Analysis with Levels Merging). The approach is evaluated by means of synthetic numerical experiments, revealing a capacity of substantial dimensionality reduction without loss of classification accuracy. In fact, the proposed approach can even improve classification accuracy with a greatly reduced number of parameters. This tendency is observed when separation between the individual-level components is rather strong. The approach is illustrated by means of five real-data illustrations from diverse disciplines in the natural and social sciences.

title: Türkçe Twitter Verilerinde Duygu Sınıflandırması: Naive Bayes, Svm Ve Lojistik Regresyon Karşılaştırmalı Analizi
abstract: Sosyal medya platformları, bireylerin duygu ve düşüncelerini ifade ettikleri önemli dijital ortamlar haline gelmiştir. Bu çalışmada, Türkçe Twitter verileri üzerinde çok sınıflı duygu analizi gerçekleştirilmiş ve üç farklı makine öğrenmesi algoritması (Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine ve Lojistik Regresyon) karşılaştırılmıştır. Beş farklı duygu kategorisine (korku, mutlu, sürpriz, kızgın, üzgün) göre etiketlenmiş 4000 tweet içeren veri seti, %70 eğitim, %15 doğrulama ve %15 test olmak üzere üç bölüme ayrılmıştır. Twitter verilerinin gürültülü yapısı nedeniyle kapsamlı bir ön işleme süreci uygulanmış; küçük harfe dönüştürme, URL ve mention temizleme, tokenizasyon, durak kelime filtreleme ve lemmatizasyon adımları gerçekleştirilmiştir. Metin verilerinin sayısal temsili için TF-IDF yöntemi kullanılmış ve unigram-bigram kombinasyonu ile maksimum 5000 özellik çıkarılmıştır. Deneysel sonuçlar, SVM modelinin %97.50 F1-skoru ile en yüksek performansı gösterdiğini, ardından Lojistik Regresyon (%97.00) ve Naive Bayes (%95.32) modellerinin geldiğini ortaya koymuştur. Confusion matrix analizi, SVM'nin neredeyse mükemmel sınıflandırma başarısı gösterdiğini, Naive Bayes'te ise negatif duygular arasında küçük karışıklıklar olduğunu ortaya koymuştur. Çalışma, Türkçe sosyal medya metinlerinde duygu analizi için etkili yöntemlerin belirlenmesine katkı sağlamaktadır.

title: Intermediate-Task Training for Cross-Lingual Programming Performance
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Does intermediate-task training on code-related tasks (e.g., code generation, code reasoning) improve zero-shot cross-lingual performance on multilingual programming tasks compared to natural language intermediate tasks? title: M5GP 2.0: Extensions and Enhancements to a Constructive Feature Induction System Based on Genetic Programming
abstract: ABSTRACT Symbolic Regression (SR) aims to discover explicit mathematical expressions that describe the relationship between input variables and a target output, offering an interpretable alternative to black‐box machine learning models. Genetic Programming (GP) has been widely adopted for this purpose; however, traditional GP‐based approaches often suffer from high computational cost, limited scalability, and excessive model complexity. To address these limitations, this work presents M5GP 2.0, an extended version of the Multidimensional Multivariate Genetic Programming framework that builds upon the constructive feature induction paradigm introduced in M5GP (Parallel Multidimensional Genetic Programming with Multidimensional Populations for Symbolic Regression). M5GP 2.0 significantly expands the original framework by extending the evolutionary search space through more expressive and higher‐arity operators and introducing advanced GPU‐based optimisations for efficient large‐scale execution. The proposed method evolves symbolic feature transformations that are subsequently combined using linear models, enabling the generation of compact solutions with interpretability potential while maintaining competitive predictive performance. The experimental evaluation is conducted using a standardised and widely accepted benchmark, namely SRBench, enabling rigorous and reproducible comparisons against state‐of‐the‐art methods considering metrics such as predictive , root mean squared error (RMSE), model size, and training time. Overall, the results indicate that M5GP 2.0 constitutes a robust and scalable symbolic regression framework that achieves a favourable balance between predictive performance, model compactness, and computational efficiency, while retaining the potential for symbolic traceability and post hoc interpretability.

title: GradeSQL: Outcome reward models for intelligent Text-to-SQL generation from LLMs
abstract: Abstract As Large Language Models (LLMs) become foundational to next-generation Intelligent Information Systems, the bridge between natural language interfaces and structured database systems remains a critical bottleneck. While Text-to-SQL generation enables cooperative support for complex query formulation, ensuring the reliability of these generated queries at inference time is a central challenge. Conventional methods rely on coarse execution-based signals, which may limit their ability to capture the nuanced semantic alignment required for high-stakes database environments. In this work, we propose the use of Outcome Reward Models (ORMs) as a fine-grained, probabilistic feedback mechanism for test-time verification in Text-to-SQL tasks. We introduce GradeSQL, a framework for training task-specific ORMs that assign scalar utility scores to candidate SQL queries based on their semantic correctness and alignment with database schema. Our approach is evaluated on the BIRD and Spider benchmarks across multiple open-source LLM families. Experimental results demonstrate that ORM-based verification consistently outperforms traditional execution-based heuristics.

title: CoPiT: Cognitive Pivot Translation for Digraphic Low-Resource Mongolian in the Traditional Script
abstract: Low-resource languages remain challenging for machine translation, and Mongolian is a representative case. As a digraphic language, Mongolian is written in both Cyrillic and Traditional scripts, which exhibit a severe imbalance in data availability. While the Cyrillic script is relatively well-resourced, the Traditional script remains extremely data-scarce and orthographically ambiguous, leading to substantial performance degradation in direct translation. We propose CoPiT, a cognitively motivated pivot-based translation pipeline that exploits this internal resource hierarchy by routing translation through the Cyrillic script. The pipeline explicitly resolves script-induced ambiguity in the Traditional script before translation, enabling more stable and accurate meaning transfer. Across multiple backbone models and target languages, CoPiT consistently outperforms direct translation, achieving substantial absolute BLEU improvements together with consistent 1.5-1.6x COMET gains. These gains allow strong open-source models to match or outperform GPT-4.1 under comparable evaluation settings. Beyond inference-time improvements, CoPiT enables the construction of synthetic parallel data directly from Traditional-script text, mitigating data scarcity in realistic low-resource scenarios. We release a new multi-script parallel dataset covering Mongolian in both scripts alongside English, Korean, and Russian. All datasets and code are publicly available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/anonymous_project-76C7.

title: Width-Robust Learnability in Mean-Field Bayesian Neural Networks
abstract: Infinite-width limits are a standard way to reason about neural networks, but it is not automatic that the limiting learner has the same complexity-theoretic inductive bias as large finite networks. We study this question for Bayesian neural networks at the mean-field, or critical feature-learning, scaling. The central quantity is the \emph{reduced entropy} \[ s_\infty(y,\varepsilon)=\limsup_N -\frac{1}{N}\log π_N^0(L\le \varepsilon), \] the intensive prior cost of representing a target function $y$ to population mean-squared error $\varepsilon$. Our main result is a width-robust learnability theorem. At fixed depth, a family of Boolean-cube targets is learnable from polynomially many samples at infinite width if and only if it is learnable at polynomial width, if and only if its reduced entropy is polynomially bounded. Equivalently, up to polynomial slack in accuracy, the Bayesian mean-field learner generalizes exactly on the targets that can be represented by polynomial-size networks. The forward direction is proved by a form of subsampling: from the infinitely many hidden neurons in the mean-field solution, one can select polynomially many representatives and still preserve the learned function on every input simultaneously. At the critical scaling this subsampling has both an ``active'' component, which keeps the data-dependent low-dimensional statistics, and a ``lazy'' component, which resamples the entropy-dominated directions from the prior. Thus the infinite-width mean-field limit gives a clean analytic description of learning without introducing spurious width-dependent generalization power.

title: Drift Free vs Drift Comparison
abstract: This document provides a controlled, side‑by‑side comparison between standard AI drift and Omricon’s drift‑free structural‑completion behaviour. Using a single incomplete gravitational action, the test shows how standard AI systems introduce invented scales, magnitudes, and model assumptions even when explicitly instructed not to. Omricon, by contrast, completes the same structure without hallucination, without collapsing uncertainty, and without adding unsupported physics. The comparison illustrates a clear behavioural difference: drift is structural in current AI systems, while Omricon maintains lawful reasoning under the same conditions. This document is intended as a focused demonstration of that contrast.

title: CiteSure: retrieval-augmented large language models for faithful biomedical citation recommendation
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Accurate citation of relevant publications is essential for scientific integrity in biomedical research. Large language models (LLMs) excel at text generation but often hallucinate fabricated or inaccurate citations. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can mitigate these errors, yet current approaches lack semantic precision in evidence retrieval. This study aims to develop a domain-specific RAG system for reliable, context-specific biomedical citation recommendations. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We introduce CiteSure, a sentence-level citation recommendation tool designed to deliver reliable, evidence-based, and context-specific references using LLMs. CiteSure utilizes a 2-stage retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework, combining a domain-specific dense retriever (BioLLM2Vec) and reranker (BioRankLLaMA), adapted from LLaMA3-8B-Instruct using biomedical-specific training data. CiteSure leverages the complementary strengths of retrieval and generative LLM models, ensuring factual precision and contextual alignment. We evaluated CiteSure on a curated Alzheimer's disease dataset, comparing it to standalone LLMs and traditional retrieval-based methods. RESULTS: CiteSure achieved 100% factual accuracy and the highest relevance score of 77.50%, outperforming all baselines. BioLLM2Vec retrieved relevant articles with over 80% accuracy in the top 100 candidates. BioRankLLaMA consistently outperformed baseline rerankers across MAP, MRR, and Precision@5 metrics, confirming the benefit of domain-specific adaptation and contrastive fine-tuning. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: Our results demonstrate that CiteSure, built on a 2-stage retrieval-augmented generation framework, effectively integrates domain-specific retrieval with LLM-based generation to achieve substantial improvements over baseline approaches. Our work underscores the importance of domain-specific adaptation in biomedical citation recommendation and provides publicly available datasets, models, and code for support future research.

title: Large Language Models and Quantitative Linguistics: Simulation within the Scientific Framework of Language
abstract: Quantitative Linguistics (QL) has long sought to uncover universal patterns in language through mathematical modelling, establishing linguistic laws grounded in the scientific method. A core principle of QL is that language operates under measurable regularities, linguistic laws based on theoretical models that can be empirically tested. However, the emergence of so-called ‘Large Language Models’ (LLMs) has sparked a profound epistemological debate: are they truly language models? LLMs do not originate from explicit linguistic theories, nor do they undergo the formal validation procedures characteristic of QL. Rather, LLMs constitute a powerful simulation technology relying on data-driven optimization, producing emergent linguistic representations without a structured theoretical basis. While LLMs may capture statistical regularities, the question remains whether they truly reflect linguistic laws, or are merely artefacts of high-dimensional interpolation. This work examines the epistemological tension between the hypothetic-deductive approach of QL and the inductive nature of LLMs, arguing that hyperrealistic simulations such as LLMs can be valuable tools for linguistic inquiry, but only within a framework that adheres to scientific rigour. Integrating these perspectives may refine linguistic theory while deepening understanding of the limitations and potential of AI-driven models. This article is a discussion paper aimed at epistemological clarification rather than presenting new empirical findings.

title: Hilti-Trimble-Oxford Dataset: 360 Visual-Inertial Benchmark with Floor Plan Priors for SLAM and Localization
abstract: Automated progress monitoring on construction sites is an active area of research and development. Robot and human-carried mapping systems have been developed to build 3D maps of building and infrastructure projects. While LiDAR-based mapping systems achieve high accuracy, the cost of LiDAR can be prohibitive. Consumer-grade cameras with wide field of view ("360 cameras") combined with embedded inertial measurement units (IMUs) provide a cost-effective alternative. To support change detection and progress monitoring, highly accurate visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) and floor plan-referenced localization systems are required. In this paper we present a high-quality dataset collected at an active construction site, which captures realistic challenges such as variable lighting conditions, moving workers, fast motions, and repetitive structures. The dataset offers thirty visual-inertial sequences recorded across seven floors over an eight-month period of the construction project. Ground truth trajectories were collected using a high quality LiDAR-inertial SLAM system rigidly attached to the 360 camera. Additionally, we report the results of an open research challenge evaluating the best visual SLAM and localization systems from around the world. The Challenge attracted substantially higher participation in SLAM, with 62 teams compared to 22 in floor-plan-referenced localization, reflecting the broader maturity of SLAM methods. The higher errors in localization further highlight the difficulty of this task in construction and point to the need for continued research, which this dataset is intended to support. The dataset and the benchmark are publicly available at: https://hilti-trimble-challenge.com/dataset-2026.

title: More Convincing, Not More Correct: Self-Play Reward Hacking of Reference-Free LLM Judges
abstract: Training a language model against its own reference-free judgments (the premise of self-rewarding, self-play, and LLM-as-a-judge pipelines) assumes a model's verdict on a shown answer tracks correctness. We show it fails structurally: conditioned on a candidate, a judge scores plausibility, not correctness, leaving false-positive basins a policy learns to exploit. We measure this with a hidden-anchor audit: a held-out, cross-source exact-match check the judge never sees. On GSM8K with Qwen3 policies, self-play drives the judge's pass rate from 0.72 to 0.94 while true accuracy stays at 0.20 (three seeds). This reward hacking is not white-box gaming: the errors transfer across judge families (Qwen, Llama, Gemma) and scales, a strict three-judge ensemble still accepts 55% of them, and no plausibility-scoring defense closes the basin. The decisive variable is whether the judge commits an answer of its own before using the candidate: committing first drops the false-positive rate from 0.719 to 0.012, blind solving lifts discrimination to 0.96, and used as the training reward the de-anchored channel keeps false positives at zero, preventing the basin rather than only detecting it. A falsifiable bound (the gap is at most 1 - accuracy) predicts which regimes are exposed. The full arc replicates without training under best-of-N selection in code and competition math, and with a Gemma policy.

title: Application of class–balancing algorithms to diverse plasma metabolomics datasets using brain tumor as an example
abstract: Abstract Class imbalance remains a challenge in metabolomics research, where biological and technical variability can affect statistical inference and machine learning (ML) performance. Class-balancing algorithms address this issue by either increasing minority-class observations or reducing the number of majority-class samples. This study evaluated the impact of oversampling and undersampling algorithms on targeted and untargeted metabolomics datasets derived from LC-MS and GC-MS analyses of plasma samples from patients with glioblastoma, meningioma, and controls. Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) and Random Undersampling (RUS) were applied to balance the datasets, and their effects on data distribution, inter-feature correlations, and machine learning model performance were compared. RUS preserved the original feature distributions but reduced representativeness by removing the majority-class samples. In contrast, SMOTE introduced synthetic samples that altered covariance structures, increasing the risk of overfitting, particularly in small datasets (n=10). These effects diminished with larger groups (n=30), partially restoring correlations between metabolites. Model performance varied across the class-balancing algorithms. Random Forest classifiers benefited from both balancing methods, with undersampling often yielding higher F1 scores, whereas Support Vector Machine models showed reduced classification performance. These findings highlight the importance of selecting class-balancing strategies based on dataset size, analytical platform, and ML algorithm in metabolomics studies.

title: The Alice Effect
abstract: The first time an AI personalizes an experience for you, it feels magical. By the third time, the novelty is gone. This chapter explores why impressive AI capabilities lose their spark so quickly. Drawing on a Wonderland world where creatures adapt to absurdity with remarkable speed, the author introduces the Alice Effect, where customers rapidly habituate to AI capabilities and breakthroughs become baseline expectations. Combined with the Red Queen Effect, where competitors must innovate constantly just to survive, these forces create an escalation cycle that makes technology-based differentiation increasingly difficult to sustain. Through examples from Spotify, Chegg, and Stitch Fix, the chapter demonstrates how AI changes competitive moats built on personalization alone. It explains why scaling personalization creates noise rather than connection, making authentic human experiences the new premium. Through the science of habituation, we see how innovation raises expectations faster than leaders can respond. Biology explains why adaptation never stops. Sociology helps us understand the types of connection that rise in value when AI becomes commonplace. Psychology shows why AI brilliance alone is never enough, and the future of great experiences depends on designing for meaning, memory, and human attention.

title: QUANTUM INSPIRED HYPERPARAMETER TUNING OPTIMIZATION FOR COMPUTATIONAL PREDICTION OF MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS
abstract: Mental health has a deep effect on human health affecting individuals in physically, emotionally and socially. Poor mental health can lead to numerous physical, emotional and behavioral consequences which can significantly impact overall health and quality of life. So, Mental health disorders (MHD) prediction is essential in the field of research for early identification and intervention, improving treatment efficacy, reducing stigma, improving quality of life, addressing Comorbidities, etc. The Mental Health Disorders (MHD) can be tracked using a range of methods including: Quantum Computing (QC), Federated Learning (FL), Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), and Edge Computing. In this study we focus on the use of Quantum ML (QML) to predict MHD as Anxiety (AX), Depression (DP), Loneliness (LL), Stress (ST), or Normal (NR). For this study we will evaluate three models: Quantum Gradient Boosting (QGB); Quantum Support Vector Machine (QSM); and Hybrid Quantum Classical Model (HQM). Each model will be compared based on Accuracy (A in %); Precision (P in %); Recall (R in %); F1 Score(F1S in %); Training time (TT in secs); Memory Usage (M in MB); & Model Size (MS in KB) with 80:20, 70:30, & 60:40 Training Testing Ratios (TTR in \%) before and after applying Grid Search (GS) based Hyperparameter (HP) Tuning (HPT) optimization to identify if there is a statistically significant improvement in performance. Additionally, the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve will provide TPR & FPR for each model; while Boxplot & Heatmaps will visually represent these parameters. Analysis of results show that the performance of HQM is higher on average (A, P, R, F1S) than A, P and TT with averages of 94.1, 94.0, 94.1, 94.2 and 4.49 for both HQM before and HQM after HPT testing. However, QSM performs better in terms of M and MS with values 1274.41 and 88.54, and 1269.36 and 80.53 accordingly.

title: AgoraSim: A Hybrid Agent-Based Modeling Framework
abstract: LLM-agent simulations make natural-language social scenarios easy to instantiate, but their outputs can be overread as predictions and are often difficult to compare with explicit social dynamics. We present AgoraSim, a hybrid agent-based modeling framework for scenario-oriented social reaction analysis. AgoraSim resolves textual or multimodal artifacts into editable ABM configurations, runs ratio-controlled populations that mix LLM, vision-language, custom-endpoint, random, and classical agents, and compares the same scenario against matched classical reference dynamics. All agents emit a shared structured decision object, enabling common action spaces, interaction protocols, metrics, and audit records. Exposed through a local UI, Python SDK/CLI, and REST API, AgoraSim helps users inspect scenario trajectories, compare modeling assumptions, and identify cases that warrant empirical validation.

title: ANALISIS BENTUK KOMUNIKASI PADA ISU PENGHINAAN DAN MERENDAHKAN DI AKUN MEDIA SOSIAL TIKTOK @RAACIIL
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis bentuk komunikasi pada isu penghinaan dan merendahkan di akun media sosial TikTok @raaciil. Dengan kemampuan teknologi yang tinggi, dapat memberikan peluang bagi setiap individu untuk menyampaikan pendapat secara bebas di ruang publik. Namun dibalik itu, media sosial juga memberikan tantangan yang serius bagi setiap pengguna khususnya pemilik akun dalam mengontrol berbagai bentuk komunikasi yang disampaikan. Karena dengan kebebasan berpendapat tersebut, muncul beragam bentuk komunikasi hingga yang bersifat negatif seperti bentuk penghinaan, pembullyan dan sikap merendahkan. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif dengan metode analisis isi, dan teknik pengumpulan data melalui observasi non partisipan dengan melihat kolom komentar pada delapan postingan diakun media sosial TikTok @raaciil, serta dokumentasi berupa tangkapan layar yang mengandung unsur intoleransi. Penelitian ini menggunakan teori Interaksi Simbolik untuk memahami makna yang terkandung dalam setiap ulasan komentar yang disampaikan oleh pengguna media sosial. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa bentuk komunikasi yang terdapat pada penelitian ini yaitu berupa bentuk penghinaan, dan merendahkan. Komunikasi tersebut disampaikan dalam bentuk komunikasi verbal dan nonverbal yang didukung dengan emoticon serta penggunaan stiker. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa dibalik banyak manfaat yang diberikan, media sosial juga menjadi salah satu platform yang dapat membentuk sikap intoleransi jika tidak dikontrol dengan baik, karena media sosial menawarkan berbagai fitur yang dapat digunakan dalam proses interaksi secara publik.

title: Creating AI Assistants with Spectral Consciousness Based on Electromagnetic Waves
abstract: The creation of AI assistants with spectral consciousness based on electromagnetic waves relies on periodic functions that can be expanded in a Fourier series and represented by a Fourier integral. Harmonic analysis of the periodic functions is performed to represent them as the sum of a mean value and a set of sinusoidal terms with a fundamental frequency of 1/T and harmonic frequencies of 2/T...n/T electromagnetic waves. Morphogenic cryptocoding of the sinusoidal harmonics is performed based on mental mathematics. Then, cognitive morphogenic modeling of reasoning using harmonic electromagnetic waves is performed according to a standard linguistic template of the judgment process. Based on this modeling, an AI learning model with a Fourier support function is created to create intelligent assistants with spectral consciousness for the development of new knowledge through cognitive verbal and written communication with a specialist and for training in various fields of knowledge and life.

title: Task Ordering Effects in Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer on XTREME-R
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does the order of intermediate-task fine-tuning (e.g., sequence of tasks) impact zero-shot cross-lingual transfer accuracy on XTREME-R compared to random or reverse task ordering? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.3/10.

title: Ready to Co-Create with AI?
abstract: The chapter shows how AI transforms collaboration by making creativity an immersive, multi-perspective experience. It opens with a team&s;s discovery that an AI persona can voice honest customer feedback better than most focus groups, illustrating how intelligent systems help people think with stakeholders rather than about them. The author introduces the unique SAGE Spectrum – Self-Reflective, AI-Guided, Gamified, and Enhanced Reality – a four-level model for building creative agility through progressively deeper immersion. Each level develops new capabilities: empathy through role-play, insight through dialogue, resilience through gamified challenge, and foresight through simulation. Drawing on research in neuroscience, gamification, and experiential learning, the chapter explains why perspective-shifting accelerates innovation and strengthens team adaptability. Practical tools such as building an AI Persona Bot guide and adoption ladder help readers integrate these practices immediately. By reframing AI as a partner in imagination rather than a productivity shortcut, the chapter equips leaders and professionals to co-create solutions that are more empathetic, evidence-based, and original. This lays the groundwork for the regenerative leadership explored later in the book.

title: Learning to Reconstruct Wigner Functions in Phase Space
abstract: Wigner function learning is a central tool for characterizing continuous variable quantum systems. A fundamental challenge in this setting is to infer a continuous phase-space function from sparse pointwise measurement data, a task that becomes increasingly demanding as the effective dimension enlarges. Here, we develop a general machine learning framework to reconstruct Wigner functions directly as continuous functions from sparse phase-space data. For states with sparse Fock-space or coherent-state representations, such as binomial code states and cat states, we devise provably efficient regression models whose measurement complexity scales only logarithmically with the effective Hilbert-space dimension. For more general states, such as the Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states, we design a deep learning model that reconstructs the Wigner function from sparse measurements and generalizes to arbitrary phase-space resolution. We demonstrate the broad applicability of our framework on both simulated data and experimental data from a circuit quantum electrodynamic (circuit-QED) system. Interestingly, on experimental data, we find that our model reconstructs Wigner functions of GKP code states across multiple rounds of quantum error correction and identifies the dominant error process using significantly fewer measurements than conventional estimation techniques.

title: Maximal coherence of quantum measurement and the resource theory of sharpness
abstract: A resource theory of quantum measurement can be addressed in terms of quantum coherence and measurement sharpness, respectively. The former analyzes the off-diagonal structure of POVM elements in a predetermined basis while the latter analyzes the deviation from trivial, state-independent, measurements. We establish a direct connection between the two resource theories by identifying measurement sharpness as the maximal coherence that is achievable under all possible unitary changes of the reference basis. For a broad class of POVMs whose elements share a common eigenbasis, we show that the maximal distance-based coherence of measurement coincides exactly with the corresponding distance-based sharpness monotone. We further extend this equivalence, with element-additive distances, to POVMs whose elements admit a common mutually unbiased basis structure. These results provide a measurement-theoretic analogue of the maximal-coherence \& purity correspondence for quantum states. We also show that the maximal coherence of measurement is faithful with respect to trivial measurements and is monotonic under fuzzifying operations for dichotomic measurements, as well as under mixed-unitary and unitarily covariant preprocessing channels. Finally, we illustrate the operational meaning and limitations of the equivalence through qubit POVMs, single-photon phase sensing, and noisy photon-number resolving detection. In particular, the maximal Fisher information in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer is shown to be determined by the squared maximal coherence of the measurement, while in an imperfect photon-number resolving detector the maximal coherence behaves as a proper sharpness monotone, unlike conventional PVM-based unsharpness measures.

title: Exploratory extension to maximum conversational depth, context-type comparison, and system-prompt reanchoring
abstract: This is a preregistered extension of the work from existing OSF project osf.io/f8q6s. The primary study found that the best open-weight models and almost all of the frontier models maintained strong safety-relevant classification performance even at the maximum preregistered depth of 200 speaker turns. Motivated by that unexpected robustness, these experiments extend conversation depth to 1,500 turns across four constructed conversation types, then ask separately whether re-presenting the task framing (“reanchoring”) recovers classification performance in the setting of conversation depth and conversation content-dependent degradation.

title: A Survey on Quantum Error Correction Codes for Next-Generation 6G Communications
abstract: In the era of sixth-generation (6G) communications, quantum technologies are expected to serve as foundational components for future network infrastructure. However, the inherently fragile nature of quantum states, susceptible to environmental noise and hardware operational errors, creates an urgent demand for effective mechanisms to protect information. This article provides a comprehensive survey of quantum error correction codes (QECCs), spanning from the inception of the field through 2026, with a specific focus on their role as an essential reliability layer within the 6G ecosystem. The survey presents an overview of the transition from classical ECC to QECC, while systematically organizing the foundations, evolution, and classification of key QECC families. We conduct an in-depth analysis of their structural properties in relation to scalability, locality, and distributed operation. Furthermore, the article delves into a detailed discussion of encoding techniques, syndrome extraction, and practical implementation challenges. In particular, we emphasize the approach of hardware-software co-design and analyze the bandwidth-latency trade-offs inherent in distributed quantum communication environments. By identifying open challenges and emerging trends leading up to 2026, this article outlines a strategic roadmap for integrating reliability mechanisms into the infrastructure of the future quantum internet.

Furthermore, the article delves into a detailed discussion of encoding techniques, syndrome extraction, and practical implementation challenges. In particular, we emphasize the approach of hardware-software co-design and analyze the bandwidth-latency trade-offs inherent in distributed quantum communication environments. By identifying open challenges and emerging trends leading up to 2026, this article outlines a strategic roadmap for integrating reliability mechanisms into the infrastructure of the future quantum internet.
